'''Seamus Casey''' (born January 8, 2004) is an American professional [[ice hockey]] player who is a [[defenceman|defenseman]] for the [[Utica Comets]] of the [[American Hockey League]] (AHL) as a prospect to the [[New Jersey Devils]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). He was drafted in the second round, 46th overall, by the Devils in the [[2022 NHL entry draft]].

==Early life==
Casey was born in [[Miami]] on January 8, 2004, to Steve and Karen Casey. When he was around the age of five the family moved to [[Fort Myers, Florida]], where he met future [[Columbus Blue Jackets]] draft pick [[Gavin Brindley]], who became a close friend and with whom he would play youth, junior, and collegiate ice hockey.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Kingsley |first=Noah |date=2022-12-22 |title=Michigan the latest step in Gavin Brindley, Seamus Casey journeys |url=http://www.michigandaily.com/ice-hockey/mini-sticks-mini-celebrities-and-married-couples-how-seamus-casey-and-gavin-brindley-blazed-a-trail-from-florida-to-michigan-together/ |access-date=2023-11-08 |website=The Michigan Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

At twelve, Casey moved to [[Detroit]] to play for the Compuware Youth Hockey AAA program.<ref name=":1" />

==Playing career==
=== Youth and junior ===
Casey was scouted by the [[Michigan Wolverines men's ice hockey|University of Michigan]] while playing for Compuware, at a game in which he was moved to [[Forward (ice hockey)|forward]] due to injuries.<ref name=":1" /> He committed to Michigan in October 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=MiHockey |date=2018-10-28 |title=Recruiting: Seamus Casey commits to Michigan |url=http://mihockey.com/2018/10/recruiting-seamus-casey-commits-to-michigan/ |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=MiHockey.com}}</ref>

Casey was drafted by the [[Sarnia Sting]] of the [[Ontario Hockey League]] (OHL), but elected instead to play for the [[USA Hockey National Team Development Program]] (NTDP).<ref name=":1" /> Had he chose to enter the OHL, he would have voided his [[College ice hockey#NCAA|NCAA]] eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baumgartner |first=Alex |date=2020-08-29 |title=Seamus Casey's journey from Estero, Florida to the US National Team |url=https://www.intermissionsports.ca/post/seamus-casey-s-journey-from-estero-florida-to-the-us-national-team |access-date=2023-11-25 |website=Intermission Sports |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2020–21 USHL season|2020–21 season]] with the NTDP, Casey's 36 points and 28 assists in 48 games ranked first among U17 team defensemen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NTDP Stats 2020–2021 |url=https://www.eliteprospects.com/league/ntdp/stats/2020-2021 |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=Elite Prospects}}</ref>

Returning to the NTDP for the [[2021–22 USHL season|2021–22 season]], he scored 33 points in 48 games, second among defensemen on the U18 team behind [[Lane Hutson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NTDP Stats 2021–2022 |url=https://www.eliteprospects.com/league/ntdp/stats/2021-2022 |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=Elite Prospects}}</ref> He was chosen as one of the top draft-eligible junior players in the United States to attend the 2023 [[USA Hockey All-American Game]].<ref name="UMich profile" /> After the season, he was selected in the second round of the [[2022 NHL entry draft]], 46th overall by the [[New Jersey Devils]], the team he supported as a child.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Amoia |first=Daniel |date=2023-07-26 |title=Devils' Prospect Seamus Casey Should Switch to Forward |url=https://thehockeywriters.com/devils-prospect-seamus-casey-should-switch-to-forward/ |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=The Hockey Writers}}</ref>

=== Collegiate ===
Making good on his commitment to Michigan, Casey joined fellow Devils draftees [[Luke Hughes (ice hockey)|Luke Hughes]] and Ethan Edwards on the Wolverines for the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's ice hockey season|2022–23 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |date=2022-07-08 |title=Michigan hockey signee Seamus Casey picked in second round of NHL draft |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2022/07/michigan-hockey-signee-seamus-casey-picked-in-second-round-of-nhl-draft.html |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=MLive.com}}</ref> He scored a respectable 29 points in 37 games, second to Hughes among Michigan defensemen, and played one game at [[Centre (ice hockey)|center]], an exhibition match against the NTDP in which he had two goals and an assist.<ref name=":0" /> Michigan won the [[Big Ten Conference]], but lost in the semifinals of the [[2023 Frozen Four]] to the eventual champions, [[Quinnipiac Bobcats men's ice hockey|Quinnipiac University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Season Ends for Michigan After Frozen Four Loss to Quinnipiac |url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2023/4/6/ice-hockey-season-ends-for-michigan-after-frozen-four-loss-to-quinnipiac |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=MGobBlue.com}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's ice hockey season|2023–24 season]], Casey recorded seven goals and 45 points in 39 games, earning [[List of All-Big Ten Hockey Teams#First Team|All-Big Ten First Team]] and [[List of Division I AHCA All-American Teams|First Team All-American]] honors. For the second straight year, Michigan won the Big Ten only to be eliminated in the [[2024 Frozen Four|Frozen Four]] semifinals by [[Boston College Eagles men's ice hockey|Boston College]].<ref name="UMich profile" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gaudio |first1=Julian |title=Two Devils Prospects Eliminated In The Frozen Four; Charlie Leddy Advances To National Championship Game |url=https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-jersey-devils/latest-news/two-devils-prospects-eliminated-in-the-frozen-four-charlie-leddy-advances-to-national-championship-game |work=The Hockey News |access-date=April 12, 2024 |date=April 11, 2024}}</ref>

=== Professional ===
Casey turned professional on May 6, 2024, after signing a three-year, entry-level contract with the Devils.<ref name="elc2024">{{cite web |title=Casey Signs Entry-Level Contract |url=https://www.nhl.com/devils/news/casey-signs-elc-release |publisher=New Jersey Devils |access-date=May 6, 2024 |date=May 6, 2024}}</ref> To start the {{nhly|2024|app=season}} and in part because of injuries to [[Brett Pesce]] and [[Luke Hughes (ice hockey)|Luke Hughes]], he made the Devils' opening night roster out of training camp, traveling to [[Prague]] for a season-opening two-game series against the [[Buffalo Sabres]] as part of the [[List of international games played by NHL teams#2024 NHL Global Series|2024 NHL Global Series]]. He made his NHL debut on October 4, 2024, a 3–1 Devils win, and scored his first NHL goal the following day, tying the game on the [[power play (ice hockey)|power play]] in the second period of the 4–1 Devils victory.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Flannery |first1=Kristy |title=Seamus Casey Scores First NHL Goal In Devils Global Series Finale |url=https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-jersey-devils/game-day/seamus-casey-scores-first-nhl-goal-in-new-jersey-devils-global-series-finale |website=[[The Hockey News]] |access-date=October 6, 2024 |date=October 5, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Trevino |first1=Gabriel |title=Devils rookie scores first NHL goal, can carve spot in crowded defenseman group |url=https://www.nj.com/devils/2024/10/devils-rookie-scores-nhl-first-goal-can-carve-spot-in-crowded-defenseman-group.html |website=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=October 6, 2024 |date=October 6, 2024}}</ref> Ten days later, in a 3–0 victory over the [[Utah Hockey Club]], he would record three more career firsts: his first assist and game-winning goal for his first multi-point game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Flannery |first1=Kristy |title=Jake Allen & Seamus Casey Lead Devils to 3-0 Victory Over Utah HC |url=https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-jersey-devils/game-day/new-jersey-devils-utah-hockey-club-seamus-casey |website=[[The Hockey News]] |access-date=October 15, 2024 |date=October 14, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Flannery |first1=Kristy |title=OPINION: Emergence Of Casey Should Lead Devils To Send Nemec To AHL Once Pesce Returns |url=https://thehockeynews.com/nhl/new-jersey-devils/latest-news/new-jersey-devils-simon-nemec-seamus-casey-brett-pesce-sheldon-keefe |website=[[The Hockey News]] |access-date=October 15, 2024 |date=October 15, 2024}}</ref>

==International play==

{{MedalBottom}}
In his lone under-18 tournament appearance, Casey represented the [[USA Hockey National Team Development Program|United States]] at the [[2022 IIHF World U18 Championships]], scoring six points in as many games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seamus Casey at eliteprospects.com |url=https://www.eliteprospects.com/player/526229/seamus-casey |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=eliteprospects.com}}</ref>

Casey traveled with [[United States men's national junior ice hockey team|Team USA]] to the [[2023 IIHF World Junior Championship]], but did not dress for any games. Michigan teammate and fellow Devils draftee Luke Hughes also attended the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-04 |title=2023 World Junior Championship rosters {{!}} NHL.com |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/2023-world-junior-championship-rosters-338699372 |access-date=2023-11-04 |website=NHL.com}}</ref> The following year, however, at the [[2024 World Junior Ice Hockey Championships]], he would be rostered,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Earegood |first1=Connor |title=USA balancing risk and reward with Buium-Casey defense pairing |url=https://thehockeynews.com/ncaa/latest-news/usa-balancing-risk-and-reward-with-buium-casey-defense-pairing- |website=thehockeynews.com |publisher=The Hockey News |access-date=March 19, 2024 |date=December 19, 2023}}</ref> and would record six assists in six games en route to a gold medal. He missed one game due to illness.<ref name="Nichols 1-5-24">{{cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=James |title=Devils Seamus Casey, Team USA Win Gold at World Junior Championship |url=https://newjerseyhockeynow.com/2024/01/05/devils-seamus-casey-team-usa-win-gold-at-world-junior-championship/ |website=newjerseyhockeynow.com |publisher=New Jersey Hockey Now |access-date=January 5, 2024 |date=January 5, 2024}}</ref>
